sources.producer_note: WHO Global Health Expenditure Database (GHED) https://apps.who.int/nha/database Last updated: April 1st, 2026 Notes: Year 2023 added for December 2025 update. Data for 2024 are preliminary and subject to revision. GHED partial update April 2026 includes updated data for Jordan (new HK values for 2020-2022), Montenegro (all classifications for 2021) and Togo (new population data 2000-2023 from UN WPP interim update and consequently readjusted per capita indicators). Other data remain the same than Dec.2025 GHED update.

sources.name: World Development Indicators

sources.coverage_note: The government finance series carrying the GC. prefix are CENTRAL government. GHED's general government expenditure is GENERAL government. Any figure that combines the two is an approximation and is labelled as one wherever it appears.

sources.name: Health Nutrition and Population Statistics
sources.citation: World Bank. Health Nutrition and Population Statistics. Washington DC: World Bank; 2025.
sources.upstream_producer: World Health Organization Global Health Observatory, financial protection database
sources.coverage_note: Every series read from this source is estimated from household surveys, not from an annual account. Surveys run every few years at best, so a country may carry a single observation in twenty years and two countries are often being compared across different years. Nothing is interpolated or carried forward to hide that.

income_groups.vintage_label: World Bank income classification as published in the GHED 2025 release (2023 vintage)

who.source_column: GHED Data sheet column region, defined in the GHED Codebook as Region (WHO)

overrides.reason: GHED files Indonesia under the Western Pacific Region. Indonesia is a member state of the WHO South-East Asia Region and has been since 1950. It is the only South-East Asia Region member state in this panel that GHED files elsewhere; the other nine are already in the region.

who.note: Every country ships two fields. who_region_source is the region exactly as the source file states it. who_region is the region this tool uses everywhere, including every group figure. They are equal except where the source contradicts WHO's own membership; those cases are listed in overrides with the reason, and there is 1 of them.

gghed_che.title: Domestic government health spending
gghed_che.subtitle: Domestic general government health expenditure as a share of current health expenditure.
gghed_che.definition: Domestic General Government Health Expenditure (GGHE-D) as % Current Health Expenditure (CHE). Method of measurement: (Transfers from government domestic revenue (allocated to health purposes) (FS.1) + Social insurance contributions (FS.3)) / Current Health Expenditure (CHE)
gghed_che.tooltip: Domestic general government health expenditure as a share of current health expenditure.
gghed_che.methodology_note: Read directly from the GHED Data sheet, no transformation.
gghed_che.producer_definition: Domestic General Government Health Expenditure (GGHE-D) as % Current Health Expenditure (CHE). Method of measurement: (Transfers from government domestic revenue (allocated to health purposes) (FS.1) + Social insurance contributions (FS.3)) / Current Health Expenditure (CHE)
gghed_che.producer_definition_attribution: WHO Global Health Expenditure Database codebook, 2025 release
gghed_che.transformation: Read directly from the GHED Data sheet, no transformation.
gghed_che.aggregation_method: median (type 7 quantile, default), unweighted mean across countries, expenditure-weighted aggregate weighted by che_usd, population-weighted mean weighted by pop

ext_che.title: External health spending
ext_che.subtitle: External health expenditure as a share of current health expenditure.
ext_che.definition: External Health Expenditure (EXT) as % of Current Health Expenditure (CHE). Method of measurement: (Transfers distributed by government from foreign origin (FS.2) + Direct foreign transfers (FS.7)) / Current Health Expenditure (CHE)
ext_che.tooltip: External health expenditure as a share of current health expenditure.
ext_che.methodology_note: Read directly from the GHED Data sheet. Rule P1 applies: where the external share is not published but the government and domestic private shares already sum to within 0.5 percentage points of 100, the external share is set to 0 and the country-year is flagged ext_imputed_zero. No other transformation.

Rule P1 applies: where the external share is not published but the government and domestic private shares already sum to within 0.5 percentage points of 100, the external share is set to 0 and the country-year is flagged ext_imputed_zero. other_pvtd_che.title: Other domestic private health spending
other_pvtd_che.subtitle: Domestic private health expenditure other than out-of-pocket payments, as a share of current health expenditure.
other_pvtd_che.definition: Derived from two GHED indicators. Domestic Private Health Expenditure (PVT-D) as % Current Health Expenditure (CHE): "(Compulsory prepayment (Other, and unspecified, than social insurance contributions) (FS.4) + Voluntary prepayment (FS.5) + Other domestic revenues n.e.c. (FS.6) + Unspecified revenues of health care financing schemes n.e.c. (FS.nec)) / Current Health Expenditure (CHE)". Out-of-pocket (OOPS) as % of Current Health Expenditure (CHE): "Household out-of-pocket payment (HF.3) / Current Health Expenditure (CHE)".
other_pvtd_che.numerator: Domestic private health expenditure minus out-of-pocket expenditure
other_pvtd_che.tooltip: Private prepaid and other domestic private sources not captured as out-of-pocket payments. Derived as domestic private financing minus out-of-pocket financing.
other_pvtd_che.methodology_note: Calculated as pvtd_che minus oops_che. A value falling in the window -0.5 to 0 percentage points is set to 0 and counted as a rounding artefact. A value below -0.5 percentage points is left as published and the country-year is flagged private_residual_negative. No other adjustment is made.
other_pvtd_che.producer_definition: Derived from two GHED indicators. Domestic Private Health Expenditure (PVT-D) as % Current Health Expenditure (CHE): "(Compulsory prepayment (Other, and unspecified, than social insurance contributions) (FS.4) + Voluntary prepayment (FS.5) + Other domestic revenues n.e.c. (FS.6) + Unspecified revenues of health care financing schemes n.e.c. (FS.nec)) / Current Health Expenditure (CHE)". Out-of-pocket (OOPS) as % of Current Health Expenditure (CHE): "Household out-of-pocket payment (HF.3) / Current Health Expenditure (CHE)".
other_pvtd_che.producer_definition_attribution: WHO Global Health Expenditure Database codebook, 2025 release
other_pvtd_che.transformation: Calculated as pvtd_che minus oops_che. A value falling in the window -0.5 to 0 percentage points is set to 0 and counted as a rounding artefact. A value below -0.5 percentage points is left as published and the country-year is flagged private_residual_negative. No other adjustment is made.
other_pvtd_che.aggregation_method: median (type 7 quantile, default), unweighted mean across countries, expenditure-weighted aggregate weighted by che_usd, population-weighted mean weighted by pop

rev_gdp.title: Government revenue
rev_gdp.subtitle: Central government revenue as a share of gross domestic product, derived from expense and net lending or borrowing.
rev_gdp.definition: Derived from two World Bank series, each quoted here as the producer defines it. Expense (% of GDP), GC.XPN.TOTL.GD.ZS: "Expense is a decrease in net worth resulting from a transaction. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period." Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) (% of GDP), GC.NLD.TOTL.GD.ZS: "Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) equals government revenue minus expense, minus net investment in nonfinancial assets." The World Bank publishes no general government revenue share of GDP; the two series above are central government.
rev_gdp.tooltip: Central government revenue as a share of gross domestic product, derived from expense and net lending or borrowing.
rev_gdp.methodology_note: Derived, not published. Calculated as GC.XPN.TOTL.GD.ZS plus GC.NLD.TOTL.GD.ZS for the same country and the same year, and left empty wherever either side is missing, so no revenue figure is ever built from half a pair. 195 country-years inside the panel carry one side only and are dropped for this series. Nothing is interpolated or carried forward. Two limits govern how far this can be read. First, coverage. These are CENTRAL government series, the World Bank GC. prefix, while the general government expenditure this tool uses everywhere else, gge_gdp, is GENERAL government from GHED. They are not the same government: general government also takes in states, provinces, local government and social security funds. Splitting gge_gdp into revenue times a fiscal stance using this series is therefore an approximation, and every surface that shows that four-factor split has to say so. The three-factor identity, GDP per capita times the government expenditure share of GDP times the health share of government expenditure, closes exactly and entirely inside GHED and needs no such caveat. Second, definition. The World Bank defines net lending or borrowing as revenue minus expense minus net investment in nonfinancial assets, so expense plus net lending or borrowing equals revenue minus net investment in nonfinancial assets. This series therefore sits below total revenue by the amount of government capital spending. Measured against GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS, Revenue excluding grants, in the same extract and the same panel, the median absolute gap is 1.384 percentage points of GDP over 3288 comparable country-years. Neither the coverage difference nor the definitional gap is corrected here.

nld_gdp.title: Fiscal balance
nld_gdp.subtitle: Central government net lending, positive, or net borrowing, negative, as a share of gross domestic product.
nld_gdp.definition: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) (% of GDP). Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) equals government revenue minus expense, minus net investment in nonfinancial assets. It is also equal to the net result of transactions in financial assets and liabilities. Net lending/net borrowing is a summary measure indicating the extent to which government is either putting financial resources at the disposal of other sectors in the economy or abroad, or utilizing the financial resources generated by other sectors in the economy or from abroad. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.
nld_gdp.tooltip: Central government net lending, positive, or net borrowing, negative, as a share of gross domestic product.
nld_gdp.methodology_note: Read directly from the World Development Indicators long extract for series GC.NLD.TOTL.GD.ZS, one value per country-year, joined to GHED on ISO3. No interpolation, no carry forward, no best-year reduction. The series is signed: a surplus is positive and a deficit is negative, so a group median can sit below zero and that is the published figure, not an error. Coverage caveat: this is CENTRAL government, not the GENERAL government that gge_gdp measures.

cat10_oop.title: Catastrophic health spending, 10 percent threshold
cat10_oop.subtitle: Share of the population spending more than 10 percent of the household budget out of pocket on health.
cat10_oop.definition: Proportion of population spending more than 10% of household consumption or income on out-of-pocket health care expenditure (%). Proportion of population spending more than 10% of household consumption or income on out-of-pocket health care expenditure. Out-of-pocket health expenditure is defined as any spending incurred by a household when any member uses a health good or service to receive any type of care (preventive, curative, rehabilitative, long-term or palliative care); provided by any type of provider; for any type of disease, illness or health condition; in any type of setting (outpatient, inpatient, at home).
cat10_oop.tooltip: Share of the population spending more than 10 percent of the household budget out of pocket on health.
cat10_oop.methodology_note: Read directly from the World Bank Health Nutrition and Population long extract for series SH.UHC.OOPC.10.ZS, one value per country-year, joined to GHED on ISO3. Nothing is interpolated, smoothed, carried forward, or moved to a neighbouring year: every figure stays on the year of the survey that produced it, and a year with no survey is empty. Read it as a survey estimate, not as an annual series. These figures come from household surveys that run every few years at best, so coverage is thin and old: within the 2000 to 2024 panel this series has 879 observations across 157 countries, the earliest in 2000 and the latest in 2021, and a country may carry only one observation in twenty years. Two countries shown side by side are often being compared across different survey years, and a country's own figures are not a trend.
cat10_oop.producer_definition: Proportion of population spending more than 10% of household consumption or income on out-of-pocket health care expenditure (%). Proportion of population spending more than 10% of household consumption or income on out-of-pocket health care expenditure. Out-of-pocket health expenditure is defined as any spending incurred by a household when any member uses a health good or service to receive any type of care (preventive, curative, rehabilitative, long-term or palliative care); provided by any type of provider; for any type of disease, illness or health condition; in any type of setting (outpatient, inpatient, at home).
cat10_oop.producer_definition_attribution: World Bank Health Nutrition and Population Statistics indicator catalogue, series SH.UHC.OOPC.10.ZS, compiled from the WHO Global Health Observatory financial protection database
cat10_oop.transformation: Read directly from the World Bank Health Nutrition and Population long extract for series SH.UHC.OOPC.10.ZS, one value per country-year, joined to GHED on ISO3. Nothing is interpolated, smoothed, carried forward, or moved to a neighbouring year: every figure stays on the year of the survey that produced it, and a year with no survey is empty. Read it as a survey estimate, not as an annual series. These figures come from household surveys that run every few years at best, so coverage is thin and old: within the 2000 to 2024 panel this series has 879 observations across 157 countries, the earliest in 2000 and the latest in 2021, and a country may carry only one observation in twenty years. Two countries shown side by side are often being compared across different survey years, and a country's own figures are not a trend.
cat10_oop.aggregation_method: median (type 7 quantile, default), unweighted mean across countries, population-weighted mean weighted by pop; no expenditure-weighted aggregate is defined for a share of population, the population-weighted mean is the weighted figure. Every statistic obeys the same CS4 rule as the rest of the payload, 8 countries and 70 percent peer coverage, and because this series is survey based most group-years do not reach it and are suppressed. That is the correct outcome and the rule is not lowered for it

che.definition: All spending on health goods and services consumed in a year. It excludes capital formation such as buildings and equipment.

gghed.definition: Health spending financed from domestic government revenue, including transfers from government domestic revenue allocated to health and social insurance contributions.

oops.definition: Direct payments made by households at the point of receiving health goods and services, net of any reimbursement.

pvtd.definition: Health spending financed from domestic private revenue, including out-of-pocket payments, voluntary prepayment, compulsory prepayment other than social insurance contributions, and other domestic revenue.

other_pvtd.definition: Domestic private health spending other than out-of-pocket payments. It is calculated as domestic private health expenditure minus out-of-pocket payments.

ext.definition: Health spending financed from foreign sources, whether channelled through government or transferred directly.

gge.definition: Total spending by general government across all functions, the denominator for the health priority indicator.

gdp.definition: The market value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year.

cfa.definition: Government schemes and compulsory contributory health care financing schemes, classified as HF.1 in the System of Health Accounts 2011.

vfa.definition: Voluntary health care payment schemes together with household out-of-pocket payments, classified as HF.2 plus HF.3 in the System of Health Accounts 2011.

shi.definition: Contributory insurance schemes for which participation is compulsory and entitlement follows from contributions, classified as HF.1.2.1.

chi.definition: Compulsory contributory health insurance schemes, classified as HF.1.2, of which social health insurance is a subset.

vhi.definition: Voluntary health insurance schemes, classified as HF.2.1.

per_capita.definition: A total divided by the resident population of the same year.

current_usd.definition: Converted from national currency at the market exchange rate of the same year, so a devaluation lowers the figure with no change in real resources.

constant_usd.definition: Converted to US dollars and deflated to the price level of 2023, so figures across years are comparable in real terms.

ppp.definition: A conversion that equalises the purchasing power of currencies, expressed in international dollars.

population.definition: Resident population, published by GHED in thousands.

tax_revenue.definition: Compulsory transfers to central government for public purposes, excluding fines, penalties and most social security contributions, as a share of gross domestic product.

gov_revenue.definition: Everything government takes in through taxes, social contributions, grants and other revenue, as a share of gross domestic product. It is the size of the pot before anything is decided about health.

gov_expense.definition: Current spending by government across all functions, as a share of gross domestic product. It excludes net investment in buildings, roads and other nonfinancial assets, so it is smaller than total government expenditure.

net_lending.definition: Government revenue minus expense minus net investment in nonfinancial assets. A positive figure is a surplus and a negative figure is a deficit.

central_government.definition: The budget of the national government alone. It is narrower than general government, which also takes in states, provinces, local government and social security funds. The two are not interchangeable, and a figure built from one cannot be read as a figure for the other.

fiscal_space.definition: The room a government has to spend more on health without putting its finances at risk. It comes from three places: a larger economy, a larger share of that economy passing through the budget, and a larger share of the budget going to health.

catastrophic_oop.definition: Out-of-pocket health payments large enough to crowd out a household's other needs. It is measured as a share of the population whose payments pass a threshold of the household budget, usually 10 percent or 25 percent.

impoverishing_oop.definition: Out-of-pocket health payments that push a household below a poverty line it would otherwise have been above. It counts people made poor by paying for care.

further_impoverishment.definition: Out-of-pocket health payments made by households that are already below the poverty line, pushing them further below it. These people are not counted among the impoverished, because they were already poor before paying.

poverty_line_215ppp.definition: The World Bank's international extreme poverty line, $2.15 a day converted at 2017 purchasing power parity. It is the same amount of money in every country, so two countries measured against it are measured against the same line.

poverty_line_relative.definition: A line set inside each country at 60 percent of median consumption, so it moves with that country's own standard of living rather than sitting at a fixed number of dollars. Two countries measured against it are not being measured against the same amount of money.

survey_estimate.definition: A figure produced from a household survey rather than from an annual account. Surveys run every few years at best, so a country may have one figure for a whole decade, and two countries are often being compared across different years.

income_group.definition: The World Bank income classification carried in the GHED release, a single 2023 vintage applied to every year from 2000 to 2024.

median.definition: The middle country value in a group, computed with the type 7 quantile definition, so a single very large country cannot move it.

aggregate.definition: The group's total spending on a component divided by its total current health expenditure, so populous and high-spending countries dominate. It is an aggregate, never an average.

unweighted_mean.definition: A simple average across countries, so every country counts equally.

pop_weighted_mean.definition: Each country's value weighted by its population, that is the value for the average person in the group.

peer_coverage.definition: The share of a group's members that published a value for the indicator and year. A group figure is shown only at 8 countries or more and 70 percent coverage or more.

pp.definition: The arithmetic difference between two shares. A share moving from 29.7 to 53.6 has risen 23.9 percentage points, not 80 percent.

suppression_rule.statement: A group statistic is computed only where at least 8 countries and at least 70 percent of the group have published a value.
suppression_rule.log_note: suppressed lists one row per suppressed group-indicator-year. Groups whose membership is already below the 8 country minimum can never pass the rule for any indicator in any year; they are stated once in suppressed_groups instead of repeating one identical row per cell. Their cells in aggregates.json still carry suppressed true, so the payload shape is uniform.

fiscal_space.statement: Government health spending per person is the product of three things: how large the economy is per person, how much of that economy passes through the government budget, and how much of that budget goes to health. A country can raise health spending by moving any one of them.

three_factor.scope: every country-year where all four series are published

four_factor.statement: The middle factor splits once more, into how much revenue the government raises as a share of GDP and how much it spends for every unit of revenue raised.
four_factor.formula: gge_gdp / 100 = (rev_gdp / 100) * fiscal_stance, where fiscal_stance = gge_gdp / rev_gdp
four_factor.caveat: This split does NOT close. rev_gdp is CENTRAL government, from the World Bank GC. series, while gge_gdp is GENERAL government, from GHED. General government also takes in states, provinces, local government and social security funds, so the two are not the same government and the fiscal stance computed from them is an approximation. Every surface that shows the four-factor split has to say so. The three-factor identity above needs no such caveat: it closes exactly and entirely inside GHED.

revenue_derivation.note: The derived series and the comparator are different quantities, so the gap is expected and is reported rather than corrected. Expense plus net lending or borrowing equals revenue minus net investment in nonfinancial assets, by the World Bank's own definition of net lending or borrowing. The comparator excludes grants in addition. The gap is therefore capital spending plus grants, and it is not an error in either series.

notes: A figure for a group of countries can be worked out three ways, and they do not agree. The median is the middle country: half the group sits above it and half below, so no single large country can pull it. That is what you see unless you change it. The expenditure-weighted figure is the group's combined spending on that component divided by its combined health spending, so large and high-spending countries weigh more. The unweighted mean counts every country once, whatever its size. Every chart says which one it is showing.

A figure for a group is shown only where at least 8 of its countries, and at least 70 percent of them, reported that year. Below that the figure is left out rather than worked out from a handful of countries. The ones that are missing for that reason are listed on the methodology page.

Health spending divides four ways: government, out-of-pocket payments by households, other domestic private spending, and money from abroad. Those four are all of a country's health spending in a year, so they always come to 100 percent, and a rise in one is a fall somewhere else.

Income groups are the World Bank classification for 2023, applied to every year from 2000 to 2024. No country changes group anywhere here, so a country that moved up after 2000 still appears in its 2023 group for the earlier years. Read an income group as a way of sorting countries, not as a record of who belonged to it at the time.

Figures per person in US dollars are converted at the market exchange rate of the year. A currency that loses value against the dollar lowers a country's figure even when nothing changed in what it spends. To follow one country over time, use the constant 2023 dollar or purchasing power parity figures in the data table.

One gap is ever filled. Where the external share is not published, but government and domestic private spending already add to within 0.5 percentage points of 100, the external share is shown as 0 percent and the year is marked. Nothing else is filled in anywhere: where a country did not report, the space is left empty.
